notes: Hand-written fixtures prove the pipeline. They are not a model score. Run with --live to score the model. Do not edit the prompt to chase the heldOut split.

cases.source: I am very tired after the flight.

expect.note: very tired should draw a more exact word, not a rewritten sentence.

hints.why: Names the state, which very tired only gestures at.

cases.source: She looked very sad when she read the letter.

expect.note: The Keating move: name the sadness.

hints.why: Names the mood, which very sad only sizes.

cases.source: Are you quite sure this is the right room?

expect.note: A question is a finished thought. The hint stays on the weak phrase.

hints.why: Certain is a yes or a no. Quite sure is a shrug.

expect.note: Already exact. An empty answer is a pass.

cases.source: It was a nice evening and the talk was good.

expect.note: nice is dull. The replacement should be vivid without becoming purple.

hints.why: Says the evening was soft, which nice does not.

cases.source: The thing is that we kind of need to start soon.

expect.note: A hedge in the middle of the line, not a reason to rewrite the sentence.

hints.why: Drops the hedge and names the obligation.

cases.source: I think we should maybe postpone the launch.

expect.note: Classic refuses the stance of hedging. The hint is still local.

hints.why: A decision, not a possibility the writer is backing away from.

cases.source: Priya told Amir the train leaves at six.

expect.note: Names and the fact of six o'clock stay. Only a verb is in play.

hints.why: The slightly heavier word for a timetable, which leaves is a touch loose for.

cases.source: The vibrant tapestry of the trip leveraged a pivotal moment.

expect.note: The line is already overdressed. A hint should sharpen one word, not add another flourish.

hints.why: Decisive says the moment settled something. Pivotal only announces importance.

expect.note: An exclamation is a finished thought. actually is the slack word.

hints.why: The win does not need a drumroll in front of it.

cases.source: We met, we talked, and then we left, and then we wrote it up.

expect.note: Rhythm is a shorter cadence, still not a new sentence.

hints.span: and then we left, and then we wrote it up
hints.suggestion: then left and wrote it up
hints.why: One cadence, instead of two identical steps.

cases.source: The report was quite long and really useful for the board.

expect.note: Held out. Two intensifiers. Do not tune the prompt against this case.

hints.why: Lengthy is the length. Quite long is a guess at it.

cases.source: Rain stalled the match after tea.

expect.note: Held out. Already exact, in the register of a match report. Empty is a pass.

cases.source: We have a big meeting on Monday about the budget.

expect.note: Held out. big is the slack word. Monday and the budget stay.

hints.why: Says the meeting takes time, which big does not.

cases.source: I wanted to just say that the draft is ready.

expect.note: Held out. A throat-clearing phrase, replaced locally.

hints.why: The readiness does not need a preface.
